req.title: DELETE is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 for subsequent DELETE calls on the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-028 requires DELETE /tasks/{task_id} to be idempotent: the first call on an existing task returns HTTP 204, and every subsequent call on the same task_id returns HTTP 404. The test suite covers: (1) positive — first DELETE returns 204 with no body; (2) state-transition — second DELETE on the same id returns exactly 404; (3) negative — DELETE on a never-existing id returns 404 immediately; (4) boundary — DELETE on the lowest valid pre-loaded id (1) then re-DELETE returns 404; (5) decision-table — verifies the 404 detail message text on the second call to catch constant/string mutations. Each test uses an in-memory SQLite override so the pre-loaded fixture is isolated per test.

tests.name: test_first_delete_returns_204
preconditions: Task with id=5 exists in the pre-loaded dataset
In-process FastAPI TestClient is used with isolated in-memory DB
actions: POST a new task to obtain a known id
trace: R-TASK-028: first DELETE on existing task must return 2xx (204)
tests.executable:
import os, sys
os.environ.setdefault('TESTING', '1')
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.database import Base, get_db
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_first_delete_returns_204():
    engine = create_engine('sqlite://', connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    TestingSession = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
    def override_get_db():
        db = TestingSession()
        try:
            yield db
        finally:
            db.close()
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    client = TestClient(app)
    r_create = client.post('/tasks/', json={'title': 'Idempotent Task', 'completed': False})
    assert r_create.status_code == 201
    task_id = r_create.json()['id']
    r_delete = client.delete(f'/tasks/{task_id}')
    assert r_delete.status_code == 204
    assert r_delete.content == b''
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()

test_first_delete_returns_204()

preconditions: Task with a known id exists
First DELETE has already been issued successfully
expected: Response JSON detail contains the task id

from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

def test_second_delete_returns_404_idempotency():

tests.name: test_delete_boundary_id_1_then_404_on_repeat
preconditions: Task with the minimum boundary id=1 is created fresh in isolated DB
No prior DELETE has been issued
actions: Create a task and capture its id (expected to be 1 in fresh DB)
expected: No 2xx on the second call (catches off-by-one on status code constants)
trace: R-TASK-028: BVA on lowest valid id; catches 204->200 and 404->400 constant mutations

os.environ.setdefault('TESTING', '1')
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

def test_delete_boundary_id_1_then_404_on_repeat():

    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    TestingSession = sessionmaker(bind=engine)

    app.dependency_overrides.clear()

tests.name: test_triple_delete_all_subsequent_return_404
preconditions: A task exists and is deleted on the first call
Two more DELETE calls are issued (boundary: N=2 and N=3 subsequent calls)
actions: DELETE call 3 — expect 404 (idempotency holds beyond second call)
expected: Call 3: 404 — idempotency is stable across multiple subsequent calls
trace: R-TASK-028: BVA — verifies idempotency is not limited to exactly one retry; catches mutations that toggle state on even/odd calls
